claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar.
The proposed WTaTiVZr specimens have a fine-grained, chemically homogeneous microstructure.
WTaTiVZr exhibits greater plastic strain than pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
WTaTiVZr exhibits greater toughness than pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
WTaTiVZr has distorted and chemically complex grain boundaries.
The distorted, chemically complex grain boundaries enhance grain-boundary sliding during high-temperature loading.
The distorted, chemically complex grain boundaries promote dislocation nucleation.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding and dislocation nucleation delay crack initiation.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding and dislocation nucleation suppress brittle fracture.
The high-entropy composition induces significant lattice distortion.
The grain boundaries have an increased density of dislocation sinks.
The proposed boundary features enable more spatially distributed plastic deformation under high-temperature loading.
Multiple slip systems contribute to deformation in WTaTiVZr under the proposed loading conditions.
The WTaTiVZr alloy will show a larger area under its stress-strain curve than pure tungsten under identical conditions.
The WTaTiVZr alloy will show more observable grain-boundary sliding than pure tungsten.
The WTaTiVZr alloy will show greater mobile-dislocation activity than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism applies only where significant recrystallization or phase segregation does not occur.
Extreme strain rates or temperatures that alter the relevant microstructure fall outside the proposed mechanism's regime.
HEA and tungsten specimens should be tested with similar grain sizes and processing histories to control microstructural confounding.
The controlled test temperature is approximately 1000–1500 °C under low-to-moderate-strain-rate loading in a chemically nonreactive environment.
